title: dfilter + ftypes: Add a "cast to double" function
description:
Add support for converting to double to the integer, time, and IEEE
11073 floating point formats. Add a display filter function that
explicitly converts fields to these types, so that the result can
be used for further calculations and, e.g., put in a column.

Also add a float function.

Fix #20219

(There might be value in having more implicit conversions, but that's
a bigger task.)

notes.body:
Does this actually address #20219? Presumably you now need to:
```
double(tcp.len) / tcp.analysis.ack_rtt
```

To confirm that this actually works as expected, can you add a test to `test/suite_dfilter/group_function.py` or similar?

I was initially concerned that this complicates the language, but the alternative with implicit conversions are not much better. For example, what if you would like `3/2` to be displayed as `1.5` instead of `1` (integer division)? We could adopt Python-style `3//2=1` and `3/2=1.5`, but that is probably not much better.

Naming was the next worry. `double` stands for "double-precision floating format". Programmers know this, not sure if it makes sense for those without that background. The name `float` might not be a good alternative for similar reasons. Without a good alternative, I suppose that `double` would be reasonable.

@SYN-bit Any thoughts on this feature and the name?

I can add a test to demonstrate that it works.

Implicit casts are a little more difficult to do in the language. It needs a rework anyway with how the implicit types work with arithmetic.

> The name float might not be a good alternative for similar reasons.

Right, I considered both alternatives, and they each have their pros and cons.

I guess if we only had a float() function, the non-programmers would understand it and the programmers would too and things are logical. But then we lose the ability to calculate with double precision. 

So would it make sense to just implement both float() and double()?
Implementing both wouldn't be too bad.

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/18116/diffs?diff_id=1186043851&start_sha=19e2de5b363d80b07c21634bc7cd89f00ebfb763)

As far as I can see, this is the first user of `fvalue_to_double` unless there are some macros somewhere.

That function will crash if the field type lacks a `val_to_double` method. Which used to be the case for all fields other than `FT_DOUBLE`. The current MR also adds support to various integer field types, but not `FT_TEXT` or `FT_BYTES` for example.

Which makes me wonder, will `double(data.data)` cause an assertion failure/crash?

The test in `ul_semcheck_double` is supposed to catch it and would in that case, but I suspect there is a problem if a field abbreviation is registered multiple times, some that support conversion and some that don't.

So there probably should be a check (possibly in other existing places) so long as we aren't verifying at registration time that non compatible field types are registered to the same abbreviation. The Code Checks CI job shows a fair amount of such fields, mostly ASN.1 and other auto generated dissectors.

Indeed, I managed to figure out a way to make it crash with the `vals()` operator and a field that is registered both as an integer with a value string and as something else with the existing baseline. Good catch.

This breaks my Windows build with Configuration RelWithDebInfo:

```
C:\wireshark\epan\dfilter\dfunctions.c(170,40): error C2220: Die folgende Warnung wird als Fehler behandelt. [C:\wireshark\build\epan\dfilter\dfilter.vcxproj]
  df_func_double(GSList *stack, uint32_t arg_count, df_cell_t *retval)
                                         ^
  
  sttype-function.c
C:\wireshark\epan\dfilter\dfunctions.c(170,40): warning C4100: "arg_count": Unreferenzierter formaler Parameter [C:\wireshark\build\epan\dfilter\dfilter.vcxproj]
  df_func_double(GSList *stack, uint32_t arg_count, df_cell_t *retval)     
```

I guess this is because `arg_count` is only used within `ws_assert(arg_count == 1);` and that gets optimzed by the compiler (see comments in [ws_assert](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsar_html/ws__assert_8h_source.html))
Thanks for the note, I'll fix it.
